title: Three-query input-consistency tester
statement: Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n>0$ input bits. Its input-consistency tester makes three nonadaptive Boolean queries, with addresses in the disjoint union of input positions and quadratic PCPP proof positions. It chooses uniformly a pair consisting of an input position $i$ and a point $y$ in the Boolean cube of dimension equal to the circuit’s quadratic variable count; it queries input position $i$ and the two linear-proof coordinates corresponding to $y$ and to $y$ shifted by the standard basis vector for input position $i$, and accepts according to the affine-consistency predicate.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean circuit $C$ on $n$ input bits
caveat: The definitions of the input-coordinate embedding, linear-proof indexing, and affine-consistency predicate are not included.
